headline: Brain-model alignment is probed via gradients, training dynamics, and EEG decoding
label: Brain Model Representational Alignment
summary: Recent preprints test whether vision and foundation models match human neural responses, exposing misalignments that performance metrics miss.
synthesis: The dominant thread is diagnostic evaluation of how computational representations correspond to human neural data, rather than headline predictive accuracy. Gradient-based mapping of DINOv3 and other vision models onto fMRI and MEG finds that backpropagated gradients mismatch the hierarchy of brain responses, asking where model and brain hierarchies diverge. A training study reports that supervised training degrades RSA alignment to human V1 fMRI across all tested biologically plausible learning rules, with an earlier PC/STDP preservation claim corrected as unsupported. EEG-FM-Audit proposes an evaluation pipeline with tuned supervised baselines and neurophysiological probing for EEG foundation models, and a co-skewness analysis finds brain foundation models lose third-order fMRI statistics without outperforming FC regression on cognition. MindAlign, by contrast, is primarily performance-oriented, reaching 54.1% zero-shot Top-1 on Things-EEG2 200-way decoding.
